reason: The text is fundamentally a narrative centered on regular human characters with extensive dialogue, emotions, and expressed opinions. Key examples include: Pharaoh (וַתִּפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ - his spirit was troubled; he speaks multiple times expressing decisions and opinions about Joseph), Joseph (וַיַּעַן יוֹסֵף - Joseph answers and interprets, expressing his views about God's role), and the chief cupbearer (וַיְדַבֵּר שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים - speaks to Pharaoh and recalls his own experience). Throughout the passage, these characters engage in dialogue, demonstrate emotional reactions, and voice their opinions about events and one another.
